pip-compile.description: The two hashed locks. Renovate reads the pip-compile command from each lock's header, bumps the pin in requirements.in or requirements-dev.in, and recompiles every lock that depends on it.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Off. It is on by default for this manager, and it recompiles both locks to move every indirect pin to its newest release, with no seven-day wait.

pip_requirements.description: Off, because pip-compile already updates the .in files, and this manager would bump a lock's pin without recompiling its hashes.

packageRules.description: compose.yaml runs this repo's own image. A bump there would merge itself, release a new version and be proposed again, compose.yaml takes the version from .env now, so this stays only as a guard.

A Python minor (3.15 to 3.16) moves everything that names the version in one PR, so the image, the workflows, the Makefile, mypy and the locks never disagree. It still waits for TJ, under the preset's Python rule.

customManagers.description: The Python version mypy checks against. No Renovate manager reads mypy.ini.
The Python a lock was compiled with, in its header. Renovate's pip-compile manager recompiles a lock under this version, so moving it moves the next recompile onto the new Python.
